reviews.author: KaleSalen
reviews.title: Amazing casual game despite misleading ads… but it has limits
reviews.text: • Summary • Advertisements make this look like a puzzle or story-choice game, but Gossip Harbor is primarily a merging game. You have to drag ingredients around a board to create new dishes. It’s enjoyable at first, but becomes repetitive over time. As you level up and unlock more dishes (and the x2 option), it takes more energy, which eventually slows progress and forces you to wait two hours to get full. You only experience the story & decorating element after serving customers and getting enough money. •• It’s best to look at the last 3 previews to get a solid idea of what the game offers, and not the rest. ——————••—————— • Plot • The game truly shines with its story. It’s engaging, mysterious, and keeps you hooked. The characters are interesting, the presentation feels genuine, and the overall storytelling is impressive. ——————••—————— • Decoration • The decoration system starts out fun but gradually feels limited (only 3 options). You are given the option to choose between the other options by tapping & holding the furniture (if available) Remember, the only way to decorate is to progress the game and serve customers! ——————••—————— • Transactions • In-app purchases are reasonably priced for what they offer (to spenders), but they’re not very useful for casual gameplay since it (⚡️) disappears quickly. Because of this, spending money can feel unnecessary and may even encourage unhealthy spending habits. Not to mention the length of each event — some are only a few hours while others are days — and luck probability. •• Game has a habit of pushing bundles out, from starter packs, to level packs. Otherwise, it doesn’t constantly shove in-app purchases at your face. ——————••—————— Conclusion: ✅ Good for casual players ❎ Not ideal for anyone wanting deep, long-term gameplay due to the limited ⚡️ system.

reviews.author: Karen Holmberg
reviews.title: False Advertising!
reviews.text: I’ll be honest. The game is decently fun to play. It’s nothing to shout at, but it’s not bad from the internal angle, especially considering there are no ads. However, the false advertising with a struggling mother and daughter cannot be ignored. What looks like an easy and “satisfying” game to play, helping a daughter and single mother in need of aid by doing simple tasks, is actually more complex and nearly baited me into purchasing items to increase progression. Fortunately, I came to my senses and uninstalled the game before that happened. If you would like to renovate a restaurant, and you know what you’re getting into and that it is NOT AT ALL like the ads suggest, then you will enjoy playing this game. However, if you found the ads enticing and are here to download, DO NOT DOWNLOAD THIS GAME!!! Development team, please either make the game like you advertise or, what I’d suggest: CHANGE THE ADVERTISEMENTS TO BE ACCURATE!!!

reviews.author: Shefgirl21
reviews.title: Separate Item Generators
reviews.text: The game has bright colors, cute yet simple animations, and a storyline that entertains a child-like curiosity. The biggest compliment is the different mini-games like the matching games within the game. The issue I have is the main game generators. The basket, for example, generates flour for bread and potatoes for fries. It is extremely difficult to get loads of flour out of the generator then get one or two potatoes when several orders call for fries. The same with the coffee/tea generator. It generators entirely more coffee than tea and it’s frustrating to spend energy constantly to get sixteen coffee cups before getting one or two tea bags. The game has a great concept but it makes me take long breaks because of the inconsistent delivery of what should be a simple, peace of mind game. Please separate the item generators to provide a more fluid gaming experience. Thank you.

reviews.author: CelticRev
reviews.title: No, It’s Not That Game
reviews.text: No, this is not that game. Regardless of what their ads say and show this is not that game where you help the poor mother and daughter in small puzzles. This is the puzzle game where you have to combine items together to level it up to another item, etc. The thing I hate the most is how much combining it takes to get the items you need to fill the orders. My level is 12 and you cannot imagine how much time and energy that took to even reach level 12. In all that time I played, I never once got the small mini game to help the mother and daughter, which I am sure is in this game at some point. When you see pictures of the mini game with the poor mother and daughter look at the level in the star as I assume those are the actual levels you need to reach to play those mini games. Needless to say I no longer play this game, so you may ask why 2 stars instead of 1. It’s still a playable game that others may enjoy. If you like waiting forever for your energy to recharge to combine item after item 50 times over this is your game. I tried to make it to the first mini game to report the level you need to reach it but got tired of it. I guess you can’t call it false advertising since I’m sure at some point you get to play the poor mother daughter mini game, but to me it is false advertising, so NO IT’S NOT THAT GAME!

reviews.author: wzrrk
reviews.title: Consuming money
reviews.text: This game starts out fun, but very quickly it becomes obvious that it is designed to make players spend a lot of money. Progress becomes extremely slow unless you keep buying gems, energy, or special items. The energy runs out very fast, and the game constantly pushes you to purchase more if you want to keep playing. Many tasks require items that take a long time to create, and when you finally get them, the rewards are very small. It feels like the game intentionally blocks your progress so you feel forced to pay. Even small actions start to require more and more resources, which makes it frustrating. What’s worse is that the in-app purchases are quite expensive, and even after spending money, it doesn’t feel like you get enough value. You can easily spend a lot and still feel stuck in the game. Overall, the game feels less like entertainment and more like a money trap. Unless you are willing to spend a lot of money regularly, it becomes very difficult to enjoy the game.

reviews.title: Beware the TOS
reviews.text: Quote from their TOS: During your use of Microfun Game Service, you shall not record or share with others the contents of Microfun Game in any way without obtaining the permission of Microfun, including but not limited to webcasting Microfun Game through any third-party software. —I’m not a lawyer, but that sounds as if they’re saying you can’t talk about the game with anyone, much less record it in anyway!? —And this: 5.16.3 Provide, at the request of Microfun, your real personal information, including your valid identity information and game information, as well as the information of other users or web games you are aware of, for example, your account and personal data under such account, login of web games and game item status, bugs and plug-ins in the application, as well as the use of bugs or plugs-in by other players you are aware of. — legally required to report others?! Wow! And of course, there is the false advertising, where they claim that they are the game helping a mother and daughter find shelter. Whoever wrote the script for the ads messed up, in my opinion, when they had the actor saying “this IS that game!” Instead of “this HAS that game”, and if anyone from the company, reading this, does not understand, they really need to consult their attorney ASAP, and change the ad in English, because that’s just straight up a lie.

reviews.author: Partyartie2209
reviews.title: Wanna Succeed? Bring $$$$
reviews.text: Okay, so admittedly, I’ve been playing this game for a while now. Unless real money is spent (which I haven’t) the game is VERY slow moving, with a lot of matching but no real movement of the game or the silly and disinteresting plot. Money comes into play with the many sub-games and contests with other players. To really make significant progress, you need to win these, but to do so, you need to BUY ENERGY. Your energy is capped at 100 and it evaporates rapidly with the large number of matches required to increase the levels of the game items. True, you may win an occasional contest or game, but more than likely you’ll be second or third and win inconsequential prizes. Note, too, the game is definitely geared to a woke audience, replete with LGBTQ relationships among the game’s characters. (Not a criticism, merely noteworthy.) More importantly, unless you’re prepared to frequently pay your way up the many in-game “ladders,” expect a very disinteresting and slogging game.

reviews.author: MinaA*
reviews.title: Not Enough Energy
reviews.text: I really love this game, it’s so fun and I truly enjoy playing it. However, I am currently on level 50 and I’m getting sick of how much energy bolts I need to simply finish 1 order. It takes 2 minutes to generate 1 energy bolt and it wont let you save more than a 100 bolts at a time, so you have to play every 3 hours to not waste energy bolts. It takes 1200 bolts to make the lobster dish, and since I only get 100 bolts max I literally have to play for 2-4 days to make it. This actually sucks, I really liked this game but it’s starting to get on my nerves so much. I hope that they change it and make it easier for us to play the game, because the game is really fun but I also don’t have the patience or time to keep checking every few hours to not waste the energy I’m given. Things that can help improve the game: 1. Being allowed to save more than a 100 energy bolts at a time (should be at least 200-300) 2. Making it cheaper to purchase dishes with our diamonds (560 diamonds for a crab dish is mental, I can make $560 irl faster than 560 diamonds in the game) 3. Allow us to choose what to generate because why do I need to generate 50 cups of coffee just so I can get 1 teacup, we should be able to choose what we want the machine to generate instead of having to waste all that time and bolts to generate a bloody teapot. Thank you and have a nice day.

reviews.author: _Katiee_
reviews.title: I use to really enjoy this game!
reviews.text: I absolutely enjoy this game! However there’s just some things that seem to not make a lot of sense. Only being able to watch ads for small things and none of the bigger stuff in the bubbles after making matches is slightly frustrating. Especially because it takes SUCH a ridiculous amount of energy just to get less than half way to the item you need. You start with 100 energy and it takes about that just to get one MAYBE two things done. Gems. You almost hardly get gems for anything and when you do get some, it’s maybe like 3-6 on the off chances you get some. The fact it takes a week OR MORE to complete orders(especially the review ones) is not fair and really starting to ruin the game for me. The little side games and stuff are the same way, you’re NEVER given enough to finish them completely or get the decent rewards. I really do like this game but these things about it are really starting to ruin it and make it boring because I literally can’t do anything except waste energy to build something that’s taking me already over a week to finish one order. I need to finish this order as it is the last one for the review thing and it won’t update to give you new ones until that one is done. Side note for anyone actually reading this, the story is absolutely nothing like the ads but it is still fun!

reviews.author: yosif wissam
reviews.title: Suggestion
reviews.text: This game is really fun and addictive. I enjoy the gameplay, the story, and the overall design—it keeps me coming back. However, there is one major issue that makes it feel unfair. As you progress to higher levels, the tasks become much harder and require a lot more energy, sometimes up to 500 energy to complete a single order. Despite that, the game still limits you to only 100 energy, which is not enough to do anything meaningful at higher levels. On top of that, the energy prices are quite expensive. Because of this, I find myself spending money on the game almost every week just to keep playing, which shouldn’t be necessary to enjoy the experience. I think the game should increase the maximum energy as players level up. For example, it could go up to 200 or more over time. Since the game becomes more challenging, the energy system should also scale with progression. Right now, 100 energy is simply not enough for advanced levels. It would also be great if the game added rewards like unlimited energy for 10–15 minutes after reaching certain goals. Features like this would make the game more enjoyable and fair, and they definitely need more development. Overall, it’s a great and enjoyable game, but these issues really need improvement to make the experience fair for players.

reviews.title: 1 star for the false advertising
reviews.text: Imagine seeing a preview for a movie, going to the theater, buying a ticket and the only thing the preview got right was the title. It seems that app developers are held to a much lower standard of advertising than other purveyors of goods. I downloaded this game assuming the bad reviews that said the ads were nothing like the game were accurate. And they totally are. But I also thought maybe those people just didn’t play long enough, maybe those levels are coming. It’s possible. I’ve only been playing for a few days so… it’s possible. I think it’s much more likely this developer just doesn’t value truth in advertising. I’ve noticed their canned response to other reviews about striving to make better games… uh, no, just don’t lie to our faces about the game. Let us choose to play the real game you created. Or not.

Considering how many times I watched a snake say “you are lying, this game does not exist” and the other snake say “no it does!!” I feel extra betrayed!! You have multiple games in this style, would it be hard to make a game that actually fits the ad? I want to keep my children warm by a fire and apply ointment in a blizzard. reviews.title: Energy takes way too long to refill.

Who wants to play a game they have to wait THREE HOURS for more energy just to use it in less than 5 minutes…. 3 hours wait time to use all my energy in less than 5 minutes . I have spent enough money on this game, but I’ve stopped because I’m literally wasting it. In order to successfully complete a craft and continue game play you’d have to spend almost $5 to $10 dollars daily… DAILY! Gas alone is $5 a gallon rn. I am not about to waste a quarter of my paycheck for a game . Energy should only take an hour to refill even an hour is an extremely long amount of time to wait. The amount of times I just forget about the game for the day when there’s a level or something I’m waiting on that has to regenerate It takes away the appeal from the game. Level is 1-15 are always fine and I’ve 2 of these games on my iPad as well and noticed that always levels one through 20 no matter which game the energy reward you get can be way higher, but then they slow down completely to the point where gameplay becomes impossible. Fix this. As developers I know you guys have noticed the exceeding decrease in gameplay after probably 6 weeks of consumers use and that I can almost guarantee is because of how long it takes for the energy to refill!!!!

reviews.author: kmurgurl
reviews.title: Bait and Switch! Don’t brother!
reviews.text: I downloaded Gossip Harbor based on the ads, and honestly, it’s incredibly misleading. The advertisements make it look like a completely different game—fun, interactive, and story-driven in a way that just isn’t reflected in the actual gameplay. What you get instead feels repetitive and nowhere near as engaging as what’s being promoted. Even more frustrating is how aggressively the game pushes in-app purchases. If you want to make any real progress or actually enjoy playing, you’re basically forced to spend money—often a lot of it. Energy runs out quickly, rewards are minimal, and progress slows to a crawl unless you pay. Overall, it feels like a bait-and-switch. The ads draw you in with something that doesn’t exist, and the game itself is heavily monetized to the point where it’s more frustrating than fun. Definitely not worth the download unless you’re prepared to spend money constantly.

reviews.author: Chowder1700
reviews.title: Review
reviews.text: This game is really fun and enjoyable, especially since it doesn’t have ads,that’s honestly my favorite part. However, I think the developers could improve the energy system. For example, it would be nice if players received free energy whenever a new day starts. Also, the energy cap is only 100, while many items require 700+ energy to create, which makes progression feel a bit too slow. Another issue is that the game constantly caps your energy at 100, which pushes players to spend money for more energy. I understand that in-app purchases are part of how games make money, and at first the deals were pretty reasonable, around $2–$3 or even $8.99. But as I progressed to higher levels, the game only started offering expensive bundles like $19 or $29, which feels a bit unfair and discouraging for players who just want to enjoy the game casually.

The end result was I was told Apple will initiate a refund, but only back to March 1st, and let me know they could see that I was being charged every time I opened the game! reviews.author: SmartWater Drinker
reviews.title: Predatory dynamic pricing
reviews.text: This game is a prime example of why regulation is necessary. You are punished for spending money. Do not spend a single cent on this app or your ability to watch ads for rewards will disappear. They also charge you more money the more you spend. The event battle pass (the one with the cat) is $3.99 for me because I’ve never purchased it. But you’ll find people online who are being charged $19.99 for it because they bought it before. This is the only game I’ve played that punishes you for supporting it. Free players actually advance more quickly than paid players. It is common for paid players to start over with F2P accounts because spending money screws you over that much. Look up strategies online and don’t give them a single dollar. Also, the story is horrible. I hate Quinn so much. I wish she were starving and freezing to death like the ads. Unfortunately for us and everyone in her orbit, she’s perfectly healthy.

People don’t walk barefoot in the snow without coats, and definitely don’t do so with their young daughters in tow. If this mom has money enough to dye her hair green, then she has money enough to buy her and her daughter some shoes and coats, even at a thrift store. I know I’m being literal, but this plot just irritates me. I think when it comes down to it, I am weary of seeing women portrayed as helpless “damsels in distress” even in a silly game. Thanks for letting me vent.

reviews.author: lin.angela
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.text: This game is really fun. More importantly though, the diversity shocked me, and I wish I was lying when I said I almost teared up. I was already shocked to see an Asian character right in the beginning (Police officer), but then to have an openly queer man who isn’t just farmed for diversity points and actually has a plot and personality, and a nonbinary character? As a queer Asian man myself I was genuinely shocked. The main character being a Hispanic single mother too, and the young girl wanting to be an astronaut… there is so much positivity and genuine struggles posed in this story in such a digestible way, that I was not expecting for a merge and match game. I haven’t seen media make diversity so normalized in a while, and was incredibly pleasantly surprised to see it here. Besides that, it’s just a fun game with no advertisements and no tricks. Amazing, highly recommend!

If you want to enjoy this game wholeheartedly, you have to be willing to spend, spend, spend. Addicting, to say the very least, in a ‘I can’t believe I’ve wasted real dollars that could’ve gone toward something useful’ way. Incredibly disappointed with myself for falling for this scheme for so long. Everything on your screen is tempting you to waste money, whether it be package deals, more gems, spins on lucky wheels, etc etc. If you have money floating around looking for something to throw it away at, this is the game for you!

reviews.title: Super fun game but beware of dynamic pricing
reviews.text: This game is visually appealing and super fun to play. You do run out of energy super easy so it’s easy to fall into micro transactions to progress. Beware that if you ever buy any of the cheaper packs of $0.99, $1.99, or $2.99, they will very rarely ever offer those as they begin only offering packs of $6.99 or more while using your data. They share data, purchase history, and other information from your device. I have all settings turned off and they still track my information. Their feedback team is also AI and only logs conversations as bugs and offers no solution. You have to provide way too much proof and videos to get any sort of reimbursement back when there is a bug. They also try to hide low reviews!

reviews.author: Elvalmeida
reviews.title: CS None exists
reviews.text: I purchase a VIP plus pass (around $10) for a few months straight and occasionally bought a few gems. What disappointed me is that after I started making purchases, I stopped receiving the “Watch Ads for Lives” option. After doing some research, I found Reddit discussions suggesting that once players spend money, this feature may be removed. I contacted customer support and explained that I was a paying customer who would appreciate having the free lives option restored. I received a generic “sorry for the inconvenience” response and was told my feedback would be passed along to the developers, but they never did nor nothing ever changed. It’s unfortunate that I have to leave this game, but the lack of response and the removal of a feature I relied on has made the experience less enjoyable. Sadly, after a few months of playing, I’ve decided to move on.

reviews.title: Could be fun, but it’s ruined by greed!
reviews.text: This game can be a lot of fun, but it’s ruined by the way they handle the micro transactions. It’s clear that their main objective is to squeeze as much money as possible out of every player, and the more you buy, the worse it gets. They literally punish you for spending money by making the game so much harder (weekly goals get way harder especially). And the offers get progressively more expensive once you start buying them. If you follow the games subreddit you’ll see that people get dramatically different offers, and even the actual gameplay difficulty varies significantly depending on your purchase history. I’d be happy to spend $10 a week or so to consistently enjoy the game, but they make everything so much worse once you start paying for anything.

Good games keep spenders well supplied with resources, this game is tailored to draining your resources and the story is unsatisfying.

reviews.author: Dig Dug....Nothing
reviews.title: Just Like Every Other Greedy Game
reviews.text: I’ve played merge games before and have gotten really into them, but the same thing keeps happening as the game is out longer and longer. The developers get greedy and start giving you less and less. The flaming frenzy was a great perk for players in this game, and started out at needing 600 coins…then went to 700…then went to 800. And now I noticed that completing dishes is giving less coins than before. It’s too bad that games can’t progress with actually offering more when more players start playing. They give you so much when the game first comes out to draw people in, but when more people start playing they make it harder to progress, thus trying to suck money out of people. Super fun game, but the next thing I’m waiting for is the refresh time for energy to raise from 2 to 3 mins. That’s what happened in the last game, and that’s when I quit.

It is a guided story (that the player cannot choose the outcome of) about the woman from the advertisements going through a divorce and taking custody of her child and restaurant that she started with her ex-husband. reviews.author: AfroSensual
reviews.title: Don't ever spend money on this game
reviews.text: I downloaded this game out of curiosity and it was not at all what was advertised. However I really enjoyed the matching aspect of the game so I had been playing for months really enjoying it. There's a ton of mini games in it which makes it interesting. They give you options for free energy and boosters by watching ads but the second you spend money on the game, like I did stupidly for a challenge (literally $1!), they take those free options away to make you keep spending money. I get that they want to make money but that's actually insane and made me sad to see because I actually really enjoyed this game. Greed will always be the downfall of mobile games! I would've spent more money on this game but seeing that it's a scam to keep you spending, I will be transitioning to a new game to play. I wish these companies would understand that we are willing to pay for game upgrades but not at the expense of being exploited for every damn penny. I can't wait until there's regulations on this because why is it so hard to find a mobile game that doesn't ultimately end up being a cash grab at every turn 😪

reviews.author: Anonymous:)101
reviews.title: Real/honest review
reviews.text: I rarely leave reviews, but I felt this one was worth writing. First, the game is nothing like the ads. To be fair, the game itself is enjoyable, but the marketing is misleading. The ads portray gameplay that simply doesn’t exist. If anything, the mechanics shown in the ads would make excellent optional side activities or mini games, and I would genuinely enjoy seeing them added. My second concern is far more significant. This is a game marketed toward children (13+), yet it includes romantic and gender-identity themes that I do not believe belong in children’s entertainment. For example, there is a scene in which Sam, a male character, makes flirtatious advances toward a male police officer, as well as the inclusion of a non-binary character using they/them pronouns. I understand that the developers may view this as an effort to promote inclusivity. However, children’s games should remain focused on gameplay rather than introducing social or ideological topics that are unrelated to the game’s purpose. Children do not need these themes woven into their entertainment, especially when they are too young to fully understand them. There is a clear difference between representing a diverse audience and deliberately incorporating contemporary social messaging into media designed for children/teens. I believe children’s games should prioritize age-appropriate storytelling and entertainment over advancing cultural or political viewpoints. Overall, the gameplay is enjoyable, but the misleading advertising and the unnecessary inclusion of these themes significantly diminish the experience.

reviews.author: abrown2019
reviews.title: Not the game Ads promised
reviews.text: Nothing special. There are countless other games very similar, and it’s nothing like the game shown in the ads. Sure, there are no forced ads, but it’s still an endless merge game built around time-locked progression and wildly overpriced microtransactions. Not the game the ads promised. At all. Will be deleting. There is no helpless mother and daughter freezing in a busted room you fix up. The CEO of Gossip Harbor is a fraud. If you want the details: The game lets you progress rapidly at first, constantly rewarding you to get you invested. Then everything slows to a crawl until you’re waiting absurd amounts of time to make any progress. That’s the business model: create impatience, then sell overpriced gems and coins for essentially time-skips as the solution. These games are intentionally designed to push players toward spending money. They create artificial obstacles and delays, then charge you to remove them. They’re just entertaining enough to keep you coming back, but deliberately frustrating enough that paying starts to feel like the easiest option. Eventually you realize you’re not paying for more fun, you’re only paying to remove problems the developers intentionally created. And they almost got me. Nice try. Oh and let’s not even get started on how Apple does not have a review interface to allow you to see anything other than what they deem “Most Helpful”. But what do we expect from a company that is heavily incentivized to, and has a long history of, profit maximizing over their customers interests.

reviews.author: cindysheindy
reviews.title: The ads for this game are disturbing
reviews.text: I’m writing this review from the ad for it that I keep being shown in other games. They are without exception disturbing and vile. The latest ad I’m being repeatedly shown has a young girl, a child of 7 or 8, outside in the snow, opening a frozen bottle of soda with her teeth. The closeup of the child’s mouth prying a metal cap from a glass bottle is so inappropriate, clearly directed at an audience that enjoys viewing harm to children (if you’ve seen any ads for this game you’ll have noticed that’s a recurring theme - harm to and violence against children and women). I don’t understand why Apple allows its Apps to show ads such as these, and almost all game ads are like this and worse, on its all ages platform. The three stars are for the ads. I’d give less but the games simply don’t post low ratings in order to falsely inflate their averages. The game is fine, if very greedy, but all games want money. The ads for it have nothing to do with the game. I can’t imagine what the developers think they accomplish by using such disturbing images to advertise a mostly innocuous game. Please for the love of little bunnies stop with these sickening ads. They have no place anywhere. Certainly not on an otherwise wholesome platform.

reviews.text: This game is fun and I enjoy the merging aspect. The ads are deceiving, you do renovate things but the mother and daughter are not in squalor and there’s no coin dropping. The worst part about this game is that you don’t get enough energy to make much, when it fully refills you max out at 100 and many of the items you need to make cost more than that. There’s not a lot of ways to get more energy other than waiting or buying it. Watching an ad only gives you 15 energy and there’s not much you can do with that. It feels like you can only play this game for a few minutes a day and then you have to wait for more energy. Of course when you play your first few levels it gives you a lot of opportunities to fill up on energy but then after level 10 you end spending more time waiting for energy than playing the game. If the energy cap was higher that would be nice and I would spend more time playing this game because it is really fun when you can actually play.

reviews.author: Qqnnyy77
reviews.title: Don’t spend money if u want fair game
reviews.text: I used to genuinely love this game. It’s a simple, relaxing merge game with great graphics, and one of the best things about it is that there are no forced ads. I happily played it every day and even spent money because I wanted to support the game. Unfortunately, after making purchases, the weekly goals became increasingly unrealistic. They started at around 220 Good Reviews, which was already difficult but achievable with patience, planning, and daily play. After a few purchases, the targets increased to 240, then 280 after I failed a week. Now I’m expected to complete 4,500 merges, earn 300 Good Reviews, collect 24,000 coins, and gather 350 cards in a single week. For a normal player, that’s simply unrealistic unless you’re spending constantly. What disappointed me the most was customer support. I reached out to explain that the weekly requirements felt impossible. The response was basically, “We’ll pass your feedback to the developers.” Instead of seeing any improvement, the goals became even harder afterward. I know that may have been a coincidence, but it honestly left me feeling like loyal, paying players are being pushed away rather than rewarded. This is still a genuinely good game with beautiful graphics and no intrusive ads, which is why this is so disappointing. I don’t mind a challenge, but the weekly events should reward dedication—not make players feel punished for supporting the game or for missing a week. Unless the progression and event balancing are made fairer, I can’t recommend spending money on this game.

reviews.author: BK don’t do it
reviews.title: It Doesn’t Reward Your Curiosity—It Monetizes It
reviews.text: After reaching Level 107, Day 126, and spending over $1,000, I can honestly say Gossip Harbor is one of the most aggressively monetized mobile games I’ve ever played. The merge gameplay is enjoyable, and the original Gnome mystery pulled me in. Unfortunately, that’s where the satisfying storytelling ends. The biggest problem isn’t the cost—it’s the lack of payoff. After the original Gnome storyline, the game continually introduces new mysteries before resolving the old ones. Characters disappear, secrets pile up, relationships change, and every story scene teases answers without actually providing them. Instead of delivering satisfying conclusions, the game keeps moving the finish line. Progress is also buried behind layer after layer of artificial delays. Energy runs out, generators recharge, high-level merge chains become increasingly tedious, coins are required to unlock story chores, and events constantly encourage spending on bundles, gems, passes, and special offers. If you want to experience the story at a reasonable pace, the game repeatedly nudges you toward your wallet. Even worse, the game’s own story recap stops at Day 50, while I reached Day 126. If the developers expect players to follow a complex mystery spanning well over 100 story days, they should at least provide a recap that keeps up. Looking back at my Apple purchase history was eye-opening. I didn’t spend over $1,000 because the game delivered $1,000 worth of content. I spent it speeding through artificial roadblocks, only to receive another small piece of dialogue that usually created more questions than answers. Gossip Harbor isn’t a bad game. It has charm, polished artwork, and an engaging premise. But it relies too heavily on stretching out the story and monetizing player curiosity rather than rewarding it. I don’t mind paying for a good game. I do mind paying over and over just to keep chasing answers that never seem to come. My rating: 2 out of 5 stars. The gameplay is fun, but the storytelling and monetization eventually turn curiosity into frustration.

reviews.author: ditsyandi
reviews.title: Money pit!
reviews.text: This game is nothing but a money pit. Sure it’s a lot of fun at first, but then you get these orders that take forever to fill if you don’t buy more gems to get more energy. Which is fine, but where they get you are these limited mini games that are impossible to win without spending money, and a lot of money. I spent 60$ trying to complete a mini game and I STILL couldn’t complete it. I just read a comment on Reddit that says even if you do spend the money it requires to complete the mini-game, the prizes aren’t even worth it. Also, you can’t get through the story without completing orders, so you’ll go days without getting the next little crumb to the story. Developers, the rewards for completing days should be better and include at least 100 energy points to make the game worth playing and the number of high level orders needs to be balanced so that players can at least get one part of the story a day. I vow to NEVER SPEND MONEY ON THESE GAMES EVER AGAIN!!! The ads to get you to play the game are not accurate at all and play on your emotions to get you to try and save this poor woman and her kids, gets you addicted, and then tries everything it can to get you to spend your hard earned dollars. DONT DO IT!! The games entire Reddit sub is people complaining on how predatory this game is.

reviews.author: Bullar2626
reviews.title: “NO ADS” — 🙄🙄🙄🙄
reviews.text: The advertisement literally says “totally FREE & AD-FREE” and “NO ANNOYING ADS.” Yet the game still shows advertisements between gameplay/levels, including promotions for other games from the same developer. Calling those “not ads” simply because they are your own games doesn’t make the experience ad-free. And honestly, the bigger problem is that the actual game is nothing like what is advertised. The advertisement gives players one impression of the gameplay, only for the downloaded game to be completely different. If you need to advertise your own games every few seconds, fine—but then don’t advertise the game as “AD-FREE.” Be honest with players about what they are downloading. “Free” and “ad-free” are two completely different promises. This game delivers neither the experience shown in the advertisement nor the ad-free experience it claims to provide. Stop misleading people with advertisements that the actual game doesn’t live up to. It’s frustrating, annoying, and makes it very difficult to trust anything else the developer claims.

I just so happened to get a red chest, personally I don’t like to use my diamonds because I like to save them for when I really need them. So I watched an ad (don’t hate on me lol) my wifi was good so I’m pretty sure it wasn’t that but the ad was loading for about 2 minutes and them my device completely shut off. I thought I just needed to update the game but I didn’t and then i no longer has the red chest. I was also really exited open the chest. I also merged into really big levels and used a lot of energy and got “lucky”. But then the items that I merged before I watched the ad were gone. Then I suddenly had more coins but then realized I had just had that amount of coins before I was reading the new gossip I had gotten so I had to redo it again. Now I do not know if this is my device’s problem but I would like to know if this has happened to anyone else. Thank You for your time!

reviews.author: Jae_r
reviews.title: Fun and engaging but costs money after a certain level
reviews.text: Starts out great and awards are simple enough to come by. The chapters start out being 20-75 coins. Then increases to 200,300, 400 plus coins to just complete one little chapter. So it’s fun but then you have to pay to play. If not, then you can play once a day for about 2 minutes and not complete any orders and maybe only complete a few orders a week. They also stop giving you decent rewards. They start out giving you 50 power and 20-40 diamonds and then sometimes no power and no gems. I have been downloading games like these and play until they start charging and then download a new game. I wish a developer would create a game that you could play that lets you do side games to refill your energy all the way. Because I’ve noticed after the game progresses you need more energy and you have to pay to play and the story line becomes dull and boring and they charge like 500 coins for a one line episode. Like Merge Restyle starts out good and they even let you play mini games to refill your energy, but it takes like 5-10 min to get like 5 energy power. And they tempt you to purchase things in the mini games too.

reviews.author: Derpington Mors
reviews.title: Big Time & Money Waster
reviews.text: Don’t play this game, it’s just not worth your time unless you love wasting your money. I found this game from ads on mobile games. This game advertises multiple times that it’s this original game that advertises you help a woman with her daughter and sometimes another child from the cold by doing these fun puzzles. When you play the game it is sadly nothing like the ads so I was kinda disappointed.. But, I didn’t mind the original gameplay. It’s a basic merging game where you have to merge items together to make certain items like food, bricks, dogs, etc for orders or quests that get progressively harder as you get further with some events sprinkled in that are very similar to other games.. the events aren’t that interesting or fun though it’s just some race or small get as many orders done as you can. This game also has a story which I tried to listen to but once you get so far ahead or locked into events, you will need to ignore the story at that point. When you are playing the game, it really wants you to be competitive and get those limited time events that last for an hour or so for something incredible items you’ll get as an reward but it is practically impossible to do it because some of the orders are just so difficult to get if you don’t have the right things to merge and so the only option you have is to buy some package deal or a pass. It does this so many times and at the start you really don’t need those deals they spam you with to make you buy something but once you get some of those insane level 13 orders with no items to help you.. It just gets too annoying too fast after that.. I really don’t recommend this game and please don’t spend money unless you’re rich because this game will 100% bleed you dry if you get addicted to it.

reviews.author: SweetGiraffe11
reviews.title: Disappointed in What This Game Has Become
reviews.text: I used to absolutely love Gossip Harbor. It was one of my go-to games, and I still like the game itself, but the balance has shifted so far toward monetization that it just isn’t as enjoyable anymore. Originally, there were two daily gifts you could collect for free. Then they added a third, made the piggy bank cost diamonds, and let you watch an ad for the energy box. I honestly didn’t mind that setup at all. I rarely depended on the piggy bank anyway, and watching an ad for extra energy felt like a fair trade. Now the only truly free daily gift is a tiny box that is mostly coins and may give you a couple pieces of energy. Even the actual energy box costs diamonds now, and when you do spend the diamonds on it, it doesn’t even fully recharge your energy anymore. That would be less frustrating if the energy demands in the game had stayed reasonable, but they haven’t. You have to spend energy to generate items and then merge them repeatedly to make the higher-level items required for orders. As you progress, you increasingly get several orders at once asking for very high-level or max-level items. You can burn through all of your energy making those items and still barely make a dent. The events are where it becomes especially noticeable. I can play for multiple days, miss completing several events because I simply cannot generate enough energy, and still not unlock another piece of the story. At that point it stops feeling like normal progression and starts feeling artificially slowed unless you spend diamonds or real money. I’ve also had glitches lately where I open a chest, receive energy as a reward, and then the energy never actually gets added to my balance. I still enjoy Gossip Harbor, which is why this is disappointing. I haven’t stopped playing, but it is no longer the game I automatically open when I have a few minutes to relax. I really wish the developers would bring back the balance the game used to have, where spending money felt optional and simply playing the game still felt rewarding.

reviews.author: Doodlebug’s mom
reviews.title: It’s not what’s advertised but it is a lot of fun
reviews.text: The ads that you see where you choose to fix a broken window or light a fire to determine if the characters survive? That’s not what this is. But it’s still a great game. I have been playing daily for many months. What it is: You choose from breads, coffees, pool floaties, seashells, etc. and use energy to produce small items. Then you match small items to make big ones. For example, two buns make a baguette, two baguettes make a loaf of sliced bread, etc. Merge items to fill customer orders, earning gold, jewels, and other items. Spend your gold to upgrade your restaurant and, ultimately, your entire property. As you do so a story unfolds where you get to know characters, build relationships, and read an unfolding mystery. Your choices are mostly “do you want this decoration in blue, yellow, or pink?” You do not choose the course of the story at all. Though I was disappointed at first that it’s not the game I thought it was, I quickly grew to love it. Here’s why: 1. Rhythm. Producing and merging items give me a nice dopamine hit by way of the rhythm that unfolds in the process. 2. Variety. There are tons of side quests. In the beginning I stuck to the primary function, but my adhd brain loves all of the extras. 3. Self-limiting. Energy accumulates over time, about one point every couple-few minutes. It maxes at 100 points, unless you are actively reaching goals that give you more. Unlike social media’s endless scroll, this produces stopping points that let me take my dopamine hit and then get back to work. 4. Truly free, truly ad-free. If you choose to stick to the imposed limits you can pop in and out of the game at intervals and play with your accumulated energy. You have options to purchase extras, either by watching ads or paying money, but neither is a requirement in order to play the game. The only drawback for me is the eleventy-bajillion pop-ups when I first open the game, or when I switch between tasks. I understand that the point of this work is for the producers to make a profit so I don’t fret about it. The side-quests are often time-limited. You’ll find it very-difficult-to-impossible to complete them without paying money. I don’t begrudge anyone their need to make a living, and I have certain places where I watch the ads in order to earn extras. You do what suits you. This really is a great game, I don’t understand the need to promote it with images and activities that aren’t in the actual game.

reviews.author: Areadien
reviews.title: Fun, but not "that game"
reviews.text: This game is fun, but it's not the advertised game as it claims to be. Certain elements are, like being (almost) ad-free (except for optimal things like more energy and such) and the mom is a divorcée. The divorce happens because Quinn finds her husband Colin surrounded by other women at a casino, but she's not unhoused or living in squalor, she doesn't have to give a baby up for adoption--in fact, she doesn't have a baby at all--and you don't use merging to help her rebuild her home. Instead, you have to rebuild her restaurant after people set fire to it, which you find out is related to food poisonings that happened there. In the process, you try to find out who set fire to it and who was behind the poisoning. I did not get that far to find out because, while the game is fun, the lying got to me. That said, if you don't mind that it's not the game it pretends to be, then it's a good game to play.

reviews.author: karara107
reviews.title: Not like the ads
reviews.text: Most games are not like their ads, which I accept, but I think it’s a special brand of crummy when ads repeatedly say “Don’t you hate it when a game isn’t like the ad? Don’t you wish you had a game that was like all those ads? Well that’s us! We’re just like our ads!” No, you’re not. I don’t generally like merge games, but was willing to give it a try in hopes it did match the ads, and because it highlighted the story as a key feature. The story makes no sense, to a degree that it feels like they changed their minds halfway through development about what they wanted the story to be, and then didn’t update all the dialogue to match the new direction. Didn’t we start by saying this was her restaurant she was running with her husband, that was then destroyed by rioters (wtf) after people were literally poisoned there? Why does she keep having to explain to people that she owns the restaurant with her husband, and doing things like introducing her daughter to her “best friend?” Haven’t they been living in this town already? Seems like the story was originally the classic moving back to your hometown and inheriting a dilapidated building, but for some reason they changed it to sabotage and possible attempted murder. In any case, it’s not at all like the ads (shocker). I played for a while anyway, but around the time the 8th or 9th concurrent “special event” popped up on the side of the screen, I realized I wasn’t actually having any fun. I was content to just delete it, but in the hour and a half total I’ve spent since then playing other games, I’ve gotten easily a dozen of their disingenuous and/or bizarrely emotionally manipulative ads telling me how this game is the one I’ve been searching for. It’s not.

reviews.author: JKT1234567890
reviews.title: Aggressive monetization
reviews.text: The graphics are great, the game is well designed, and I really enjoy the variety of events and mini-games. I also appreciate that there are no ads. Unfortunately, the aggressive monetization takes away a lot of the enjoyment. Many limited-time events seem intentionally designed so that regular energy regeneration and normal gameplay are simply not enough to complete them within the given time. You can make some progress for free, but if you want to actually finish the event and earn the main reward, you are constantly pushed toward buying diamonds, coins, energy, or one of the many packages being offered. I understand that mobile games need to make money, but there should be a reasonable balance. Players who spend time playing consistently should still have a realistic chance to complete events without having to spend significant amounts of money every time. It’s disappointing because this could be a really enjoyable game. The graphics and content deserve more than one star, but the excessive pay-to-progress design does not.

Beyond level 20 you are going to need more taps than you could ever earn organically in a day to get some of the orders done. I calculated that on x4 you need about 7 taps of the tackle box just to get to the smallest item anyone requests. That comes out to 28 energy for the smallest. That’s 56 for the next level and then 112 for the level after that. For those following along that brings you to the “pasta pescatore” and from there there are 4 more levels to the “seafood tower” so double the taps for each subsequent level. Then there are challenges and side games which might get you extra energy or some dishes but you’ll never get to finish those challenges without buying more energy or gems. Frustrating. I’d rather watch ads.

reviews.author: GothieBarbie
reviews.title: QOL Improvements Needed
reviews.text: I’ve been playing this game for quite a bit, it’s really entertaining and there’s always opportunity to get more energy. Not to compare, but if it was a bit more like Travel Town I think I’d enjoy it more. You don’t get rewarded for discovering new merger items, you can’t trade cards and it’s almost impossible to fully complete an album unless you’re spending money, the weekly challenges are difficult to accomplish I’ve never been able to finish all tasks and the limited timed events seem to end way too quickly. I’m not sure if it’s a fear tactic to get you to spend money due to FOMO but it sucks to miss out on rewards because of it. You can’t add friends on the game and I’m pretty sure team up events are done with bot accounts. Other than that, the story is really interesting and I love decorating as I progress throughout the game. If these things were worked on it would not only be a good competitor but more people would play. Overall they have better rewards than Travel Town but they don’t really mean much if you can’t complete the tasks due to the difficulty and time needed.

reviews.author: Amerissá
reviews.title: Age verification
reviews.text: I love this game. It's the only game that's survived my mass app deletions over the years, but now I'm being asked to verify my age through k-ID by uploading my driver's license or a photo of my face. I'm already signed in through Apple to protect my account and game progress. Surely there should be a way to use an existing, trusted account or another verification method rather than requiring players to submit sensitive personal information. I understand that there may be legal or regulatory requirements the developers need to follow. However, I live in GA in the US, and I haven't found a law that requires players of a mobile game like this to upload their ID or face. If this is legally required, please explain which law applies. I'm also uncomfortable being directed to a third-party website that assures me my information isn't retained. That's a promise I'm expected to trust with my government-issued identification or facial image, and I don't feel comfortable taking that risk just to play a mobile game. I love Gossip Harbor, which makes this especially disappointing. But I'm not uploading my driver's license or face to continue playing. Please offer players a less intrusive way to verify their age and a clear explanation of why this information is necessary.

Some of the orders require using a producer that takes an hour to recharge (the orange tree). One producer is a dog house. I’ve been playing for 2 weeks (not 24/7, but some each day) and I’m not even to the next to last product. When you level up, you get pieces of producers that are already on the board instead of a new producer. So, you may have multiple coffee makers but keep the same few producers for the same old order. I would prefer adding new producers and retiring the old ones. Once you’ve completed the same order for a week in a row, it’s time for new orders. Didn’t love it. Deleting it.

reviews.author: Micheleonel
reviews.title: FALSE ADVERTISED GAME! Do NOT bother downloading!
reviews.text: Do NOT BOTHER DOWNLOADING THIS APP. The developers are trying to lead you to a destination where you will NEVER arrive. It is such a SCAM! The developer has created these intriguing and VERY compelling ads where you believe you are going to save the woman and her children from the bitter cold or other dangerous situations. You will NEVER save the woman BECAUSE THE GAME DOESN’T EXIST! It makes ZERO SENSE for these app developers to put such effort and incredible expense in creating the ILLUSION of a game, claiming to have thousands of levels and situations, only to then present a simple merge game where users will never find and save this woman. It’s DECEITFUL and, quite honestly, is a direct reflection on the LACK OF INTEGRITY AND CHARACTER of those who claim their ads are a real game. (And there is no doubt MANY of those 5-star reviews are PAID for!) To the developer: What is the point? Why must you LIE to your customers? Why not OFFER THE “damsel in distress” as REAL GAME? You’ve already gone through the expense of creating it for these ads. WHY ISN’T IT A REAL GAME??? I CAN ALREADY HEAR THE DEVELOPER’S REPLY. They will NOT address the fact that their advertised game doesn’t exist. Instead they will thank me for my feedback and how they will strive to create better games. They will also say that they will communicate with their advertisers to optimize their ad content. You see? They won’t even accept responsibility for their own decisions. The reality is this: their advertisers create the ads they are paid by the developer to create. The game owners are the ones who make the decision to run the deceptive ads and to mislead users in the hopes they will download the app and play their simple, average and uninspired game. They bring shame to themselves and they don’t seem to care….otherwise they’d change what they are doing.

reviews.text: I am finally writing a review of this game because I am sick and tired of seeing the ads. I first saw the ads and of course, figured I’d give it a try. Come to find out, the exacts things they preach in those are ads are what they themselves are doing. “All those games that are nothing like the ads. Not Gossip Harbor.” No, it is Gossip Harbor too. You don’t help save this mother and child from a snowstorm. Her husband cheated on her, they divorced and someone wrecked her restaurant. So, it’s your job to help her by merging the items in the game, fixing things, and trying to find out who did it. While the game itself is entertaining at first, it eventually became boring for me and I got more and more irritated seeing the ads when I knew it wasn’t anything like they picture it to be. All in all, don’t get your hopes up. The ads are bull- and if what you are expecting is a game exactly like the ads show, it’s not. I would say those ads have maybe 5% truth to them. Gossip Harbor, if you’re going to keep chanting about how amazing your game is, maybe make the ads actually match instead of lying to your audience.

reviews.title: Real review
reviews.text: Okay, so for starters this game is definitely fun. The organizing and matching really make this game what it is. HOWEVER, there is absolutely no way to enjoy the game and progress consistently without paying for energy and gems. The game is designed to give you a dopamine hit that makes you feel like you need to play it and you need to pay for the little packages they offer. The game get progressively more complicated and the only way to enjoy playing is to keep purchasing packages. The levels get extremely hard to pass, side quest get extremely difficult and you’ll begin getting frustrated because you want to play/pass a level but you won’t be able to with out paying. So, tread lightly with this game.

reviews.author: Gypy1$1
reviews.title: Not what they advertised
reviews.text: I downloaded this game specifically because of the side-story adventures advertised in the ads, where you help a girl set up her home, renovate rooms, and fix things. However, after downloading and playing, I quickly realized that these features are not what the actual game delivers. The side adventures shown in the advertisements are clearly being used as bait to get people to download the app, and that is extremely misleading. I have no issue with a game being different from what I expected, but I do have an issue with false advertising. If you are going to promote specific gameplay features to attract players, those features should actually exist in the game as advertised. I eventually stopped playing, but seeing these same misleading ads repeatedly pushed me to finally write this review. It is frustrating, deceptive, and honestly disappointing. I also intend to look into reporting this app for misleading advertising. Developers need to be held accountable for advertising a game that doesn’t deliver what it promises. I wonder if there’s a way to report this to Apple app control

reviews.author: MiyoMeOhMy
reviews.title: GIVE ME A REFUND
reviews.text: It’s NOT as advertised. The mom and kid are NOT poor and dirty in tattered clothing. Besides that, the plot is written like a teen wrote it. Our protag is weird and wishy washy and has the attention span of a goldfish. I could forgive all of that because the merging aspect is not as dumb as other merge games. Cupcake becomes a small cake becomes a large cake and then a larger cake. Makes sense. Unlike other games, the merging makes sense. I could forgive that the events do not give you enough time to finish them (for free anyway.) And I could forgive that there is only 100 energy and ONLY ever 100 energy allowed to be recharged because you can somewhat manage to play well for a while. What I CANNOT forgive is that this game is impossible to play the longer you play it. The 100 energy limit is absolutely awful for higher levels— you barely have enough to start any order cuz the orders become impossibly larger. And the game doesn’t throw you much freebies that you can merge to help you reach say, the giant Lvl 10 lobster meal or whatever because they give you the small Lvl 1-5 things. The rewards for most things are hardly worth the effort too for mini games and mini events! I feel like I need at least 200 energy to get anywhere at the game level I’m at: 30+. I’ve even spent money a little to get farther in events and not even that helps— I wish I had a refund cuz I feel dumb for thinking those little packs would get me far into any event. The game basically begs you to pay money at higher levels and I don’t forgive any of this stuff. I’m starting to regret playing it— and I feel like starting over itself isn’t a good idea either. No wins here at all. Smh. I hate how I have like 8 gems, unlocked the bonus reward thing, and I have mostly nothing to show for it. Btw don’t do the weird Story Mode quests— they are a waste of energy and a waste of time. The rewards suck! And merging to the rocketship or dog or whatever takes so long that the tiny reward won’t be worth it. Overall, I wish I had my time and money back. I liked the merging and yes there is no ads but that’s it. Ugh. LIKE. I WANT A FULL REFUND BRO.

reviews.author: Carnalogist
reviews.title: It’s ok
reviews.text: There was a time where you’d get items to merge and they’d pop out another item of the next level in an ice cube. Say you combine two level 7 sandwiches and sometimes you get a random level 8 sandwich from it. This level 8 sandwich would be in a cube. That cube with a level 8 sandwich had approximately 5 minutes or so before it dissolved and turned into a coin. Within that time frame, if you can level another sandwich to level 8 and combine them together, it would give you an instant level 9 sandwich. A latest update flipped that and now it turns into a lower level item instead of the next level up. So when you combine a level 7 item, now you’ll get a lower level item of 6 instead of 8. It’s the little things that they do that purposely slows down your progress, I don’t purchase anything from this game anymore, I used to do the monthly booster pass, not anymore. You can get everything for free in this game with just normal play, the game is designed to make you buy diamonds progress faster, it’s not really necessary at all to spend any money on this game and I wouldn’t recommend playing this game because of the changes the developers have made.
